title: 2013 HMMT November Guts Problem 13
statement: Let \(S=\{1,2, \ldots, 2013\}\). Find the number of ordered triples \((A, B, C)\) of subsets of \(S\) such that \(A \subseteq B\) and \(A \cup B \cup C=S\).

solutions.text: \(5^{2013}\) OR \(125^{671}\) Let \(n=2013\). Each of the \(n\) elements can be independently placed in 5 spots: there are \(2^{3}-1\) choices with element \(x\) in at least one set, and we subtract the \(2^{1}\) choices with element \(x\) in set \(A\) but not \(B\). Specifying where the elements go uniquely determines \(A, B, C\), so there are \(5^{n}=5^{2013}\) ordered triples.
